newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bridgecon sees 40-50 mln rgt profit.
newsitem.headline: Bridgecon sees 40-50 mln rgt profit.

text.p: Civil engineering firm Bridgecon Bhd said on Tuesday it expects to report a pretax profit of 40 to 50 million ringgit in calendar year 1998.
"We expect to see 40 to 50 million ringgit gross pretax profit in '98," Hashim Mahfar, executive director of Bridgecon, told a news conference after the company's annual general meeting.
He said the group was expecting to make a pretax profit of 25 million ringgit in 1997. In 1996, Bridgecon reported pretax profit of 15.91 million ringgit.
He said the bulk of the profits in 1997 would come from its construction activities, but that by 1998, property development would contribute about 50 percent of group profits.

The company on Tuesday also said it is proposing the development of a 4,200 acre mixed-use property project in central Selangor state. Development of the township is expected to cost 3.6 billion ringgit.
Total sales value for the project is forecast at 4.6 billion ringgit, the company said.
The township is expected to be developed over 20 to 25 years.

Discussing Bridgecon's involvement in Putrajaya, the site for a proposed new federal capital outside Kuala Lumpur, Bridgecon said it will develop the central boulevard measuring four km by 100 metres.

Raduan Mohd Taib, Bridgecon executive chairman, said the boulevard would cost around 370 million ringgit. He said the group was developing a total of 500 million ringgit worth of projects in the Putrajaya development.
Raduan said the remaining 130 million ringgit would be spent on the development of roads and "other infrastructure jobs".
Bridgecon intends to change its name to Bridgecon Holdings Bhd.
